falsifier: Any function under GC/1.2.5 where a call result assigned to a named local coalesces into a later call's argument register with no intervening move - which would show the assignment is not always a barrier - or, conversely, any function where converting such an assignment to a nested subexpression leaves the object byte-identical, which would show the nesting does not reach the decision point. On DoTexModSeqSub specifically: if `python tools/gdl/fndiff.py game/g3d/auxanim.c DoTexModSeqSub --ops` at 5d54341d8 ever reports `ours-only: -1 fmr` again with the nested form in place, the nesting is not what removed the move and this law is disproved on its headline instance. The corollary about block scope is disproved by any measurement where block-scoping the staging local removes rather than adds an fmr.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: When a call's return value is passed straight on to a second call, MWCC decides where it lands from the SOURCE FORM, and only two forms exist: a named local staged through an assignment, or a nested call subexpression. The named local gets a stable home chosen for its whole web and is then COPIED into the argument register at each use; the nested form coalesces the result directly into the argument register the second call needs, emitting nothing. The choice is not reachable by scope, declaration position or declaration count - only by the nesting itself. MEASURED on game/g3d/auxanim.c::DoTexModSeqSub at commit b31bad6fa, -O4 with the demo cflags. `r = CalcTexScroll(de, ra, fr2, frame, &out); MBTreeSetUVScaleAdd(out, r, 1.0f, 0.0f, ctx, 1);` emitted `@0xac fmr f0,f1` (the result parked in r's home f0) and then `@0xc0 fmr f2,f0` at the call, against the target's single `@0xac fmr f2,f1` - one surplus instruction. Rewriting the two arms as `MBTreeSetUVScaleAdd(out, CalcTexScroll(de, ra, fr2, frame, &out), 1.0f, 0.0f, ctx, 1);` and `MBTreeSetUVScaleAdd(1.0f, 0.0f, out2, CalcTexScroll(de, ra, fr2, frame, &out2), ctx, 1);` removed BOTH surplus moves at once: real 110 -> 85 and the opcode multiset's `ours-only: -1 fmr` went to `(none)`. THREE COROLLARIES, each measured on the same function. FIRST, the two non-nested spellings are the same allocator decision: block-scoping `r` inside each case arm made it WORSE, not better - a second `fmr` appeared at @0x140 in the arm that had matched, real 110 -> 133 and count parity was LOST at O202 - and moving `r`'s declaration to the end of the function-scope list was NEUTRAL-REARRANGED at real 110. So the cross-arm web is not the cause and shortening it is not the cure; the assignment is. SECOND, the nested form's argument-load ORDER is the tell that identifies it in the target before any probe: the target loads the OTHER arguments AFTER the inner call returns (`bl CalcTexScroll` then `lfs f1,24(r1)` then the constants), because the buffer the inner call writes is read in the same expression. A target that loads all arguments before the inner call is NOT using the nested form. THIRD, the nesting reads a local in the same expression that passes its address to the inner call, which looks like an evaluation-order hazard and is not one here: MWCC evaluates the inner call first and the target's own byte order is this form.
